title: Micro-signal review playbook (scratch)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, informal notes for handling very small PRs (<= 150 LOC) with an emphasis on safety, speed, and minimizing churn. This is a personal scratchpad — experiments, heuristics, TODOs.

Context / problem statement:
- Small PRs are frequent and often low-risk, but they add cognitive load when reviewers treat them like large changes.
- We want consistent, fast outcomes: merge vs. request small follow-ups vs. request revert.
- Need to codify signals and lightweight checks so reviewers can make predictable calls.

Heuristic checklist (fast path) — single-pass reviewer (~3–6 min):
1) Surface signals (scan):
   - Files touched: predominantly tests/docs/chore -> bias to approve with note
   - Touches core runtime or deployment config -> escalate to slow path
   - New dependencies? -> no-go for fast path, request dependency rationale and SEC check
2) Tests: quick skim for smoke tests changed/added. If test-only change: approve + merge
3) Type safety / compile: does CI pass? Flaky CI recent? If yes, add inline note + hold merge until green
4) Behavioral diffs: search for public api changes (exported functions, request/response shapes). Any change -> slow path
5) Comments: small fixes with clear intent -> approve. If intent unclear -> request 1-line explanation

Fast-path rubric (explicit):
- If LOC <= 150 AND (files are docs/test/chore OR only a single small function) AND CI green AND no new deps AND not in runtime/serving code -> APPROVE with short comment.
- If LOC <= 150 but touches serving-runtime OR infra config (k8s manifests, helm, infra-as-code) -> move to SLOW PATH.

Slow path (5–30 min):
- Add reviewer label 'slow-path' and @owner tag
- Run local smoke if possible (commands below)
- Cross-check linked tickets (JIRA) and design notes
- If change touches model serving or request routing, ping SRE/infra for eyeballs

Suggested local commands (mac/linux):
- ./dev/run-smoke --file <path>  # quick local smoke harness (stub)
- git show --stat origin/pr/<n> | sed -n '1,200p'
- rg "TODO|HACK|FIXME" <path> || true

Typical PR comment templates (copy-paste friendly):
- Approve: "LGTM — small change, CI green. Merging when green unless objections (cc @owner)."
- Approve + note: "Approving — one small optional nits below. No blockers."
- Request quick follow-up: "Can you add a one-line test or note in changelog? I'll re-approve after."
- Request slow-review: "This touches runtime-inference; moving to slow-path for one more reviewer (cc @eng-sre)."

Mini-algorithm for triage bot (sketch):
- Input: PR metadata (files_changed, total_loc, labels, new_deps, owner_team)
- Score = 0
  - +2 if any file in (runtime/, infra/, private-deployments/)
  - +1 if new dependency added
  - +1 if tests modified
  - -1 if only docs or only tests
  - +2 if LOC > 300
- If Score >=2 -> suggest slow-path; if Score <=0 -> recommend fast-path; else human decision

Follow-ups / experiments to run (short list):
- Run 30-day retrospective: measure time-to-merge for PRs <= 150 LOC before/after applying rubric
- Create lint rule to flag new deps in PR description automatically
- Add a tiny GH action that posts a suggested rubric label (fast/slow) based on the mini-algorithm

Edge cases / gotchas:
- Changelogs: some docs-only PRs required for release note correctness — still do quick review for formatting
- Flaky CI: recent flakiness can hide regressions; if flakes within last 24h, be more conservative
- Binary diffs: treat as slow-path unless trivial (version bump in package.json only)

Personal TODOs (scratch):
- [ ] Prototype GH action and test on a low-traffic repo
- [ ] Draft a short write-up for eng-reviews channel explaining fast-path vs slow-path (1 paragraph + examples)
- [ ] Collect 50 sample PRs and annotate decisions for training the triage bot

Quick notes to self / one-liners:
- When in doubt: prefer revertability (small follow-up over a risky merge)
- Keep reviewer comments short and action-oriented
- Encourage authors to add a 1-line rationale for any change touching runtime infra

Example quick-approve comment (tiny template):
"LGTM — small change, CI passed. Merging on green. If you want a follow-up, open a new PR for the nit listed below."

Who to ping for runtime/infra: @noelle (SRE), @ava (serving-runtime), @marcus (infra)

End of scratchpad.

-- Sahil
